text:
ivan: Quick onboarding/help ask — I'll be doing an on-site customer demo from a laptop on the customer's network and want to know whether to use a hosted key or a sandbox/demo key. We're worried about the customer's firewall/NAT and hitting 429s or breaking streaming. Who should I contact for a short hosted bump, and is there a checklist I should send to their IT so streaming isn't blocked?
onboard-bot: Welcome Ivan! :wave: For demo quotas DM demo-ops or post here with the demo window. See the demo guide in the handbook: https://redwood.dev/onboarding.
demo-ops: Hi @ivan  we usually recommend a sandbox/demo key for customer on-site demos (separate quota, fastest to provision). If you need the hosted environment for fidelity, we can request a short hosted bump but that requires approval from Growth/Billing for customer-facing demos. If you want hosted, include demo date/time, expected QPS, and whether it's streaming or embeddings.
ivan: Sandbox sounds fine — the customer cares about latency but not exact infra. What should I give their IT to whitelist?
infra-security: For on-prem/customer firewalls, ask their IT to allow outbound TLS to `api.redwood.ai` and to avoid buffering or terminating chunked responses for streaming endpoints. Provide them our published egress CIDR (internal link) and request that the proxy not mutate `Authorization` or strip `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`. Also ask them to not coalesce many clients behind a single NAT if possible (IP NAT bucket issues).
dev-support: Quick pro tip: if their network NATs many devices to one IP, you can still use sandbox keys but you may hit IP-level buckets. For demos, we can issue an isolated demo VM or give you ephemeral Vault creds tied to a single IP if the customer can white-list one host. DM me and we'll pick the lowest-friction option.
ivan: Here's the curl I plan to use. Is this okay to run on-site?
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-demo-REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream -d '{"model":"rwd-1-small","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}' -v
```
If I get a 429 during the demo, what should I capture?
sam: If you hit a 429 capture the response headers (redact the token): `x-rate-limit-remaining`, `x-rate-limit-reset`, `x-request-id`, and `retry-after` if present. If you see connection resets capture the curl stderr (`Recv failure: Connection reset by peer`) and the `x-request-id` when available. Those let us trace the gateway and see whether it was token quota, IP bucket, or network.
demo-ops: If you prefer zero risk, we can: 1) issue a sandbox/demo key valid for the demo window, 2) create ephemeral creds via Vault bound to a single VM IP you control at the customer site, or 3) request a hosted bump (takes longer). Which do you prefer?
ivan: Sandbox/demo key + hotspot test first. If that fails due to NAT we'll explore the VM option.
ops-bot: Reminder: do not paste secrets in channels. Use placeholders when sharing requests.
infra-security: One more operational note: some customer proxies downgrade HTTP/2 to HTTP/1.1 and buffer frames; for debugging force `--http1.1 -N` in curl to see if that helps. Also ask IT to increase idle timeouts for long-lived streams.
ivan: Thanks everyone, DMing demo-ops for a sandbox key and will run a hotspot test and a forced `--http1.1` run. Will paste `x-request-id` if I hit a 429. Appreciate the help :thumbsup:
